previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A man with a history of systolic heart failure, atrial fibrillation, COPD, and alcohol dependence was admitted for chest pain, dyspnea, and an oral abscess after his medications were stolen. He developed acute on chronic heart failure exacerbation due to non-compliance, with pulmonary edema and volume overload, managed with IV diuresis and restarting home heart failure medications. His chest pain was determined to be non-ischemic, and he was restarted on metoprolol for atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular rate. An oral abscess was drained twice and treated with antibiotics. He showed signs of alcohol withdrawal, managed with symptom-triggered benzodiazepines, but left against medical advice with ongoing withdrawal symptoms. His kidney function declined mildly, likely due to diuresis, and he was discharged home with close follow-up instructions.
problems: Acute on chronic systolic heart failure
Personal history of noncompliance with medical treatment, presenting hazards to health

Brief Hospital Course:
Mr. ___ is a ___ year old male with PMH of COPD, CAD s/p

ACUTE ISSUES:
# Atypical Chest Pain in setting of CAD and CHF ___: Pt with 
significant cardiac history with multiple PCIs presents with 
chest pain and mild SOB after binge drinking and not taking 
medications. ProBNP elevated to 4353 with mild pumonary edema on 
CXR. Patient given 40mg IV lasix in the ED given signs of CHF. 
After diuresis he felt much better but still had occasional 
chest pain without EKG changes. Concern for costochondirits 
given sharp stabbing nature and atypical onset with resolution 
despite intervention. EKG without changes and trops negative x3. 
He was resumed on home lisinopril 10, Spironolactone 12.5, ASA 
81, torsemide 60 and fractionated metoprolol to tartrate 25 BID. 
He was discharged on all of his home medications. 

# COPD: Pt with history of COPD, diffusely wheezing on exam at 
admission, administered duoneb with significant improvement. now 
improved significantly. sating high ___ on RA without evidence 
of acute COPD exacerbation. Restarted home 
Fluticasone-Salmeterol Diskus (500/50)  1 INH IH BID, Tiotropium 
Bromide 1 CAP IH DAILY.

# bilateral foot pain: Upon presentation the patient described 
significant bilateral foot pain that inhibited walking. There 
was initial concern for infection in the ED so he got 1g 
vancomycin. upon arrival to the floor he was assessed by 
podietry who determined that there was no infection and no need 
for surgery. X-rays were negative for osteomyelitis. Given 
history it is likely chronic pain from multiple amputations and 
neuropathy. Discharged on lyrica and ultram. Treated with 
morphine 15mg Q6H PRN during admission and ultram. Not 
discharged with narcotics for pain due to high potential for 
abuse. Discharged with Ultram 50-100mg Q4-6H for pain not to 
exceed 400mg. Stopped gabapentin as paitient has side effect of 
stuttering at higher doses. 

# Recent GI Bleed / suprapubic pain: Recently left AMA from 
___ for GI bleed reports BRBPR. Possible bowel herniation 
given worsening with food, infection unlikely given normal white 
count and no fever. Patient denies bleeding since he left 
___ and states that a supra-pubic bulge adjacent 
to an old appendectomy scar has since resolved. Ultrasound did 
not reveal any evidence of bowel herniation. He was monitored 
carefully and ultimately discharged on omeprazole 40 daily.

# Alcohol abuse/Homelessness: Pt with long standing h/o alcohol 
abuse states that he is ready to go to a program to get sober he 
does not want to feel this way anymore. Recently loss brother to 
alcoholism. Upon admission he was placed on CIWA, continued on 
thiamine and folate. He did not go through severe withdrawal and 
was taken off CIWA after 24 hours. He was connected with social 
work and discharged to a shelter with resources.

CHRONIC ISSUES:    
# Atrial fibrillation: Pt with h/o atrial fibrillation, in a-fib 
on admission. Continued home rivaroxaban and monitored on 
telemetry without acute event. Metoprolol was continued as 
above. Discharged on metoprolol XL 50 mg and rivaroxaban because

# Hyperlipidemia: continued atorvastatin as above
# Anxiety: continued home BuPROPion (Sustained Release) 150 mg

EXAMINATION:  Chest radiograph.

INDICATION:  ___ male with chest pain and shortness of breath.

TECHNIQUE:  Frontal and lateral view of the chest.

COMPARISON:  Comparison is made to chest radiograph ___.

FINDINGS: 

Mild-to-moderate cardiomegaly is unchanged.  Linear right basilar opacity most
likely represents atelectasis.  There is mild vascular congestion.  There is
no pleural effusion or pneumothorax.  There is no acute osseous abnormality.

IMPRESSION:


1. Stable cardiomegaly.
2. Mild vascular congestion.
3. Right basilar linear opacity, most consistent with atelectasis, followup as
clinically indicated.

EXAMINATION:  FOOT AP,LAT AND OBL BILATERAL

INDICATION:  ___ year old homeless alcoholic man with bilateral foot pain, s/p
multiple amputations  // please assess for bilat osteo vs fractures

COMPARISON:  None.

FINDINGS: 

Right foot:  Compared with the prior study from ___, the patient
has undergone amputation or less likely interval destruction of the previously
abnormal phalanx of the third toe.   There is mild surrounding soft tissue
swelling, less than on the prior study. As before, there are only 2 phalanges
in the second toe and the distal surface of the second toe is flattened. 
Allowing for this, the distal surface of the second toe does appear less
distinct and subtly eroded on today's exam, concerning for early
osteomyelitis.  In addition, compared to the prior study, the morphology of
the distal phalanx of the great toe is different, with a more truncated
tapered appearance to the distal tuft.  Degenerative changes and probable
subchondral cysts of the lateral first MTP joint are again noted, similar to
the prior study.  A subtle well corticated erosion along the medial aspect of
the first proximal phalanx near the IP joint is unchanged the raises the
question of a subtle gouty erosion.

Left foot:  Compared with ___,  partial amputation of the first
through fifth toes appears similar to the prior study.  No new superimposed
erosive changes are identified.  Lobulated, relatively well corticated erosion
at the lateral base of the third metatarsal could also represent a gouty
erosion.

IMPRESSION:


1. Right foot:  The middle/ distal phalanx of the third toe is no longer
visualized --question interval amputation.
2. Right foot:  Subtle indistinctness of the distal edge of the second toe --
in the appropriate clinical setting, this appearance is compatible with early
osteomyelitis.
3. Right foot:  Interval change in morphology of the distal tuft of the right
first toe --question postoperative.  Unusual bony resorption, e.g.
acro-osteolysis, might also account for this appearance and therefore clinical
correlation is requested.
4. Left foot:  Doubt significant interval change.  No new erosion identified.
5. Both feet:  Relatively well corticated erosion along the medial aspect of
the right first proximal phalanx and at the lateral base of the left third
metatarsal raise the question of gouty erosions.
6. No acute fracture detected in either foot.

with suprapubic pain worse with eating.  // please assess for ventral

Transverse and sagittal images were obtained of the superficial tissues of the

IMPRESSION: 

No evidence of hernia, fluid collection or abdominal wall defect.
